info.title: biohub-tracking-src
info.subtitle: Reusable Python package for 3D+time cell detection, tracking & submission
info.description:
# biohub-tracking-src

Source code (the `biohub_tracking` Python package) for a 3D+time cell-tracking
pipeline built for the **Biohub – Cell Tracking During Development** competition.
This dataset exists so the code can be imported inside a **Kaggle notebook with
internet disabled** — you attach it as an input and `import biohub_tracking`.

## Context
The competition asks you to detect cells in 3D microscopy volumes over time, link
them across frames, and reconstruct cell-division lineages, scored by edge Jaccard
+ 0.1 × division Jaccard. Voxels are anisotropic (z=1.625, y=x=0.40625 µm), labels
are sparse, and submission notebooks must run offline within 12 hours.
## What it does
A tracking-by-detection pipeline that keeps detection and linking as separate,
auditable stages, with every spatial decision made in physical (micron) space:
- **data/** – lazy Zarr volume reader (one timepoint at a time) + sparse `.geff`
  ground-truth graph reader + a metadata-only dataset probe.
- **geometry** – voxel↔micron conversion and anisotropy-aware distance/gating.
- **detect/** – classical local-maxima detector (no weights) and a 3D UNet heatmap
  detector trained from sparse point labels, with micron-unit non-max suppression.
- **link/** – physical-space Hungarian frame-to-frame linking into a lineage graph.
- **submit/** – streaming `submission.csv` writer (exact competition schema) and an
  end-to-end per-dataset pipeline (detect → link → write).
- **experiments/** – offline experiment registry (config, metrics, reproducibility
  lineage), plus resumable training with dataset caching, EDA reporting, and
  metric-progress plots.
## Why it's needed
Kaggle rerun notebooks have no internet, so custom code can't be `pip install`ed —
it must be attached as a dataset. This package lets a lightweight submission
notebook do inference only, producing a valid submission within the runtime limit,
while the (optional) trained weights are attached separately.
## How to reuse it
```python
import sys; 
# auto-locate the attached package
from pathlib import Path
src = next(Path('/kaggle/input').glob('**/biohub_tracking/__init__.py')).parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(src))
from biohub_tracking.submit.pipeline import run_submission, classical_detector
run_submission(
    test_dir='/kaggle/input/biohub-cell-tracking-during-development/test',
    out_path='/kaggle/working/submission.csv',
    detector=classical_detector(),   # or swap in a trained-model detector
)
